/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 01 May 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2730 (44)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4447 (120)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2002 (10)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1520 (-5)
Baltic Handysize Index: 815 (1)
CAPESIZE
It has been a relatively quiet but ultimately constructive end to a shortened week, with participation thinned by Labour Day holidays across a number of regions. Despite the lighter activity, underlying sentiment remained firm, allowing the market to close on a positive note. The BCI 182 5TC index gained $1,087 on the day to finish the week at $40,331. The C5 index continued its gradual upward trajectory, rising by $0.227 to $13.667, while the C3 index posted a stronger move, climbing $0.595 to $35.050, reflecting improving conditions in the South Atlantic. In the Pacific, sentiment was positive throughout, supported by a tightening tonnage list, particularly for May loading C3 cargoes where ballaster supply remains constrained. Although only one miner was active on C5 today, fixtures from the previous day continued to underpin the market. Notably, a cargo for 14 May arrival was fixed at $13.99, highlighting a premium for earlier laycan. Offers today were reported in the high $13s, with trades discussed in the mid-$13s and indications edging towards $13.90 by the close. The Atlantic, while quieter following a more active midweek period, maintained a positive undertone. South Atlantic activity showed continued traction, with C3 fixtures consolidating in the mid-to-high $34s to $35 range, narrowing earlier spreads.
PANAMAX
Reported fixture activity was subdued amid several Labour Day holidays, with trading predictably thin and limited business reported. Contrary to the usual pattern in quieter markets, sentiment tilted more positively across both basins. Brokers cited a healthier fronthaul book, especially from North Coast South America, while noting that tonnage availability ex North Continent and West Mediterranean are beginning to tighten. The net result is the P2A increased by $319 to $24,794. Market participants have stated that mineral supply within the Atlantic remains thin but with the positive outlook for P2A it has been suggested by some that this may start to have a positive impact for transatlantic rates. In Asia, a token amount of fixtures were reported but with robust Australian coal export volumes continuing to make headlines the market is in anticipation to see what the next week brings. The P5TC concluded the week at $18,018 rising by $88.
SUPRAMAX
With the widespread holiday both in the Atlantic and Pacific regions for those who remained at their desks it was a a rather slow day with little excitement coming to light. The Atlantic brokers said moost areas had gone into a holding pattern with no clear direction forthcoming. Brokers said from the US Gulf fundamentals remained the same whilst from South America little fresh enquiry added a bit of negative sentiment into the mix. The Asian arena also lacked impetus with a trickle of fresh enquiry being outstripped by the amount of prompt tonnage. The Zalea Rising (56,625 2010) open Campha was heard to have been placed in the mid $19,000s for a trip China with nickel ore, but no more details surfaced. The 11TC average finished the week down $69 at $19,209.
HANDYSIZE
The week wrapped up on a largely flat note, largely influenced by the 1st of May holidays across most loading regions. The BHSI settled at 815, while the 7TC ended the week at $14,666. Both the Continent and Mediterranean regions experienced a rather quiet day, with most participants maintaining a positional stance and little movement in rates. The South Atlantic continues to be sluggish, as rates lingered around previous levels. In the US Gulf, even though a few decent fixtures were reported, the abundance of tonnage available across most loading areas prevented any significant rate improvements. Over in Asia, the market remained slow, as regional holidays kept activity subdued and rates mostly unchanged from prior levels.

Atlantic
The Yasa Kyoto (37,396 2023) was reported failed for a Panama City to UK-Continent trip with wood pellets at $16,000 by Lauritzen. The Manta Kerem (37,046 2015) also failed for a Mobile to India coal trip at $18,000 by Aries Bulk, though the same vessel was later heard placed on subjects for a clean trans Atlantic trip at $14,000 by Lauritzen, further details remain undisclosed.

Asia
The Federal Pride (42,686 2023), open Phu My 30 April was heard placed on subjects to Far East with salt at $17,000 by Kline. The HPC Liberty (31,881 2010) open Singapore fixed for a trip via Kendagawang to EC India, passing Penang with alumina in the $13,000s, though additional details were not shared. Additionally, a 33,000 open SE Asia was reported placed on subjects for Malaysia to China at around $12,000, but specifics are still lacking.

Market Fundamentals
Fertilizer Markets Under Strain as Supply Disruptions Drive Volatility

Fertilizer markets remain under severe pressure as unresolved Middle East tensions and the Strait of Hormuz blockade reduce effective shipping volumes by an estimated 80-90%, according to CRU. Bulk Ammonia prices continue to climb amid tight global supply, up $13/t on the week to ~$890/t CFR NW Europe as of 30 April, according to CRU. Sulphur has recorded further triple-digit weekly increases, up $105/t to ~$830/t CFR China. Urea prices have eased after India purchased 2.5 Mt for delivery through mid-June, with bulk Urea FOB New Orleans price down $19/t to ~640/t in the week ending 30 April.

US Weekly Grain Exports

In the week to 23 April, US combined exports of corn, wheat, soy (beans and meal) and sorghum dipped 0.5 Mt from the prior week to 3.2 Mt, USDA data show. This came as exports declined of corn (-0.3 Mt to 1.6 Mt), wheat (-0.1 Mt to 0.3 Mt) and soy (beans+meal) (-0.1 Mt to 1.0 Mt). Conversely, sorghum shipments remained near steady on the week at 0.2 Mt.

Trading Commentary
Cape
Cape had a very quiet start to the month, but the week ended with stronger sentiment as rates pushed higher across the curve. May traded down to a low of 36500 before being bid up to 37000. June saw a larger move, rising from 33750 to 34650, before settling around 34250. Q3 traded within a narrow $200 range at 30500–30700, while the Q3+Q4 strip printed at 30400.There was no participation on the cal today.

PMX
Laboured liquidity in the PMX market, with many participants out for Labour Day public holiday. Buyers pushed the curve higher against a lack of offers, May trading 19350 – 19650, Jun 19850 – 20150 and Jul 19500 – 19700, while Q3 traded between 19100 – 19300. Q4 traded 17400 – 17500 and Q1’27 at 14100. Cal27 found a level, trading a few times at 14800.

SMX + HANDY
A positive start to the month for SMX paper as the front traded up $200, but on thin volume, trading under 1000 lots for the day. May traded between $17550-$17500, valued at $17450 at close. Jun traded up to $17750, before closing at $17650. Q3 was the most active, trading between $16900-$17100, and closing at the highs. Q4 featured only a couple of times, between $15500-$15600.

Carbon
EU carbon markets ended almost unchanged as May Day holidays kept futures trading volume below 10m EUAs. Despite the lower volumes, the market rallied over �75/eua on the benchmark Dec26 contract before falling back to �73.95/eua, up 0.2%, during the assessment window. Additional holidays on Monday, including in the UK, suggest that volumes will remain low until Tuesday, although the market remains sensitive to developments in the Arabian Gulf.

Market Fundamentals
Fertilizer Markets Under Strain as Supply Disruptions
Drive Volatility
Fertilizer markets remain under severe pressure as
unresolved Middle East tensions and the Strait of Hormuz
blockade reduce eﬀective shipping volumes by an estimated
80-90%, according to CRU. Bulk Ammonia prices continue to
climb amid tight global supply, up $13/t on the week to
~$890/t CFR NW Europe as of 30 April, according to CRU.
Sulphur has recorded further triple-digit weekly increases,
up $105/t to ~$830/t CFR China. Urea prices have eased after
India purchased 2.5 Mt for delivery through mid-June, with
bulk Urea FOB New Orleans price down $19/t to ~640/t in the
week ending 30 April.
US Weekly Grain Exports
In the week to 23 April, US combined exports of corn, wheat,
soy (beans and meal) and sorghum dipped 0.5 Mt from the
prior week to 3.2 Mt, USDA data show. This came as exports
declined of corn (-0.3 Mt to 1.6 Mt), wheat (-0.1 Mt to 0.3 Mt)
and soy (beans+meal) (-0.1 Mt to 1.0 Mt). Conversely,
sorghum shipments remained near steady on the week at
0.2 Mt.
Trading Commentary
Cape
Cape had a very quiet start to the month, but the week
ended with stronger sentiment as rates pushed higher
across the curve. May traded down to a low of 36500 before
being bid up to 37000. June saw a larger move, rising from
33750 to 34650, before settling around 34250. Q3 traded
within a narrow $200 range at 30500–30700, while the
Q3+Q4 strip printed at 30400.There was no participation on
the cal today.
PMX
Laboured liquidity in the PMX market, with many participants
out for Labour Day public holiday. Buyers pushed the curve
higher against a lack of oﬀers, May trading 19350 – 19650,
Jun 19850 – 20150 and Jul 19500 – 19700, while Q3 traded
between 19100 – 19300. Q4 traded 17400 – 17500 and Q1’27
at 14100. Cal27 found a level, trading a few times at 14800.
SMX + HANDY
A positive start to the month for SMX paper as the front
traded up $200, but on thin volume, trading under 1000 lots
for the day. May traded between $17550-$17500, valued at
$17450 at close. Jun traded up to $17750, before closing at
$17650. Q3 was the most active, trading between
$16900-$17100, and closing at the highs. Q4 featured only a
couple of times, between $15500-$15600.Cape 180 5TC

Carbon
EU carbon markets ended almost unchanged as May Day
holidays kept futures trading volume below 10m EUAs.
Despite the lower volumes, the market rallied over €75/eua
on the benchmark Dec26 contract before falling back to
€73.95/eua, up 0.2%, during the assessment window.
Additional holidays on Monday, including in the UK, suggest
that volumes will remain low until Tuesday, although the
market remains sensitive to developments in the Arabian
Gulf.

The ongoing tensions in the Middle East, particularly concerning the Strait of Hormuz,
have resulted in increased restrictions on the movement of tonnage, creating further un-
certainty across the commodity markets. Shortages within both the oil and gas sectors are
continuing to have a knock -on effect across the shipping industry, including the ship recy-
cling sector.

Despite these challenges, sentiment remains broadly positive, with enquiry continuing to
be seen across all of the Indian Sub Continent markets. Price levels do vary, with Bangla-
desh continuing to lead, followed by Pakistan, with India trailing, although the differential
is not particularly significant. India does, however, retain a clear advantage when it comes
to specialised and HKC -compliant tonnage, with virtually all recycling yards now fully com-
pliant.

The persistent issue remains the ongoing shortage of available tonnage, which has result-
ed in a slowdown in fresh sales, with previously concluded transactions once again coming
to the forefront of market reporting.

The sanctioned VLCC “Mali” (39,388 lwt), which had earlier been refused entry into Paki-
stan and was subsequently reported as heading towards Sharjah, has now arrived in
Alang, India. It is assumed that the vessel has now satisfied the enhanced documentary
requirements imposed by the local authorities and has been granted clearance in prepara-
tion for delivery.
Meanwhile, uncertainty continues to surround the two OFAC sanctioned VLCCs “Itaugua”
and “Shelif”, both of which were previously refused entry into Bangladesh. No confirmed
sales have yet been reported for either vessel, although market speculation has suggested
their presence offshore Chattogram. However, latest position data appears to contradict
this, with the “Shelif” currently reported at anchor in the Persian Gulf, while the “Itaugua”
is indicated to be in the South China Sea.

The Capesize “Jin Jiang” was originally reported sold for recycling in March, with the Own-
ers having secured the option to trade the vessel further prior to resale. Now renamed
“Jiang”, the vessel has surprisingly arrived in Bangladesh following a subsequent resale on
private terms. This change in direction is likely reflective of the significant improvement in
pricing seen in Bangladesh over the past month. No resale price has yet been disclosed.

Looking ahead, the market appears to be delicately balanced. While underlying demand
from recyclers remains firm and pricing has shown resilience, the lack of available ton-
nage continues to limit overall activity. Should supply begin to return, particularly in the
form of larger units, competition between yards could quickly intensify, supporting further
firming of price levels. Much will depend on the broader geopolitical backdrop; however, if
stability improves and owners regain confidence to release vessels, there remains poten-
tial for a more active and competitive market in the weeks ahead.

India’s Crude Oil Imports Fall To All -Time Low
India’s crude oil imports from the Middle East Gulf dropped by 1.95M b/d m -o-m and by 1.28M b/d y -o-y to 1.18M b/d in March, the
lowest on records dating back to 2012, according to Reuters tanker arrivals data. Shipments from North America and Latin Amer ica
also declined by 60K b/d m -o-m to 160K b/d and by 180K b/d m -o-m to 130K b/d respectively. Meanwhile, arrivals from the FSU
rose by 1.27M b/d m -o-m to 2.36M b/d, while volumes from West Africa grew by 130K b/d m -o-m to 500K b/d. Overall crude oil im-
ports fell by 800K b/d m -o-m to 4.49M b/d, an eight -month low.

ARA Gasoil Stocks Drop To Lowest Level Since August 2025
At the Amsterdam -Rotterdam -Antwerp (ARA) storage hub, gasoil stocks declined by 20KT w -o-w to 1.84MT during the week ending
30 April, the lowest since August 2025, according to data from Refinitiv. Meanwhile, jet fuel inventories also dropped by 30K T w-o-w
to 550KT, the lowest since March 2020, whereas gasoline stocks were up by 40KT w -o-w to 1.15MT. Total clean product stocks re-
mained relatively stable w -o-w at 3.93MT.

Fertilizer Markets Under Strain as Supply Disruptions Drive Volatility
Fertilizer markets remain under severe pressure as unresolved Middle East tensions and the Strait of Hormuz blockade reduce e ffec-
tive shipping volumes by an estimated 80 -90%, according to CRU. Bulk Ammonia prices continue to climb amid tight global supply,
up $13/t on the week to ~$890/t CFR NW Europe as of 30 April, according to CRU. Sulphur has recorded further triple -digit weekly
increases, up $105/t to ~$830/t CFR China. Urea prices have eased after India purchased 2.5 Mt for delivery through mid -June,
with bulk Urea FOB New Orleans price down $19/t to ~640/t in the week ending 30 April.

US Weekly Grain Exports
In the week to 23 April, US combined exports of corn, wheat, soy (beans and meal) and sorghum dipped 0.5 Mt from the prior we ek
to 3.2 Mt, USDA data show. This came as exports declined of corn ( -0.3 Mt to 1.6 Mt), wheat ( -0.1 Mt to 0.3 Mt) and soy
(beans+meal) ( -0.1 Mt to 1.0 Mt). Conversely, sorghum shipments remained near steady on the week at 0.2 Mt.

Handysize/Supramax Report1st May 2026
63,500 Atlantic: SOFTER      Paciﬁc: FIRM           38,000 Atlantic: FLAT      Paciﬁc: FLAT
Atlantic Comment
The Baltic Dry Index (BDI) has extended its upward trajectory to close out April, hovering
near 2,670 points and driven by a robust Capesize segment where daily earnings remain
exceptionally high at over $35,000. The market's upward momentum is supported by strong
iron ore and mineral ﬂows from both the Atlantic and Paciﬁc basins ahead of the May Day
holidays. However, the operational reality for shipowners remains volatile as bunker fuel
prices act like a rollercoaster, swinging wildly in response to ﬂuctuating crude prices and
ongoing Middle East tensions, meaning that these strong headline freight revenues are
being continually squeezed by the unpredictable cost of refueling.
In the Continent Handysize market, the week opened with a quiet start and activity has
remained limited since. Fixing levels for a transatlantic voyage have stayed ﬂat at $9,000,
the same level as last week. For the Supramax and Ultramax sizes, rates have held ﬁrm,
supported by a relatively tight tonnage list, with ﬁxing levels for a transatlantic voyage up
from last week at $10,500.
The Mediterranean market has seen rates remain largely ﬂat overall with little fresh enquiry
failing to match a long tonnage list for both the smaller and larger sizes. While ﬁxture
volume has been thin, we heard that a 35k deadweight vessel ﬁx basis Annaba for a trip to
Malaysia for region $10,500 – 11,000. For the larger sizes, activity remained subdued, but
despite this, ﬁxing levels for a transatlantic voyage held ﬁrm at $10,500, up slightly from
last week.
The East Coast South America (ECSA) Handysize market ﬁrmed up noticeably again this
week, though the recent momentum risks outpacing actual demand as owners push their
rate expectations too far. While sentiment remains robust, a noticeable lack of fresh
cargoes has created a disconnect, leaving charterers hesitant to meet the elevated levels
being requested. Furthermore, a lingering supply of available vessels remains visible across
the basin, meaning owners' attempts to push for higher rates may prove overextended.
Unless fresh inquiries enter the market to absorb the remaining prompt tonnage, the
recent ﬁrmness could stall, creating a more balanced or even softening environment as the
week draws to a close. The ECSA and West Africa (WAFR) Supramax and Ultramax market is
easing slightly moving into mid-May. While steady Brazilian grain and mineral ﬂows provide
some underlying support, charterers are successfully testing lower levels against the
weight of the current tonnage overhang. In the West Africa region, the market remains
somewhat positional. Ultramax units ﬁxing from West Africa to the Continent are currently
achieving between $17,000 and $17,500, while fronthaul routes are holding a relatively
ﬁrmer tone, yielding between $21,000 and $22,000. Meanwhile, ECSA rates have softened.
Fixtures to the Continent have slipped to around $24,500 though business directed toward
the East Mediterranean is holding up slightly better, ranging closer to $27,000 to $27,500.
Overall, the market remains on a mild downward trend, and its next direction will depend
on fresh cargo volumes stepping in to absorb the available supply.
It's been a fairly quiet week in the USG Handy Market. Rates have remained largely
sideways, however there is underlying positive sentiment as we could potentially see an
increase in tonnage/cargo next week as people return from holidays and the Geneva Dry
Conference. The USG Smx market has lethargically drawn to a close after a ﬂat week.
Geneva Dry took a good chunk of players out the game and rates have been slowly tailing
oﬀ after some strong transatlantic numbers reported on Monday. We saw a 64 deadweight
vessel ﬁx basis Mississippi River for a trip with grains to Spain at for $28,000. We have seen
more fronthaul cargoes in the market this week, a mixture of grains and minerals. Nice
Japanese Ultras have covered around the $24,000 level over the last few days whilst TA
cargos have been less abundant than in previous weeks. A lot of operators are using own
tonnage for their cargos and the tonnage counts indicate we will see excess tonnage supply
for 1h May which will impact the rates negatively.

Handysize/Supramax Report1st May 2026
Paciﬁc Comments
This week, the Paciﬁc Supramax market showed signs of moderation following last week’s sharp rally, with overall momentum easing to some extent. The release of
fresh cargoes was relatively limited, and with the approaching Labor Day holiday, charterers turned more cautious, leading to a noticeable cooling in the aggressive
tonnage-ﬁxing sentiment. While owners generally remained conﬁdent, some prompt vessels softened their oﬀers slightly to secure employment. As a result, the
market experienced a mild correction rather than any sharp downturn, and overall levels remained elevated.
The Indonesian coal sector softened this week, with fewer fresh cargoes entering the market and rates easing from previous highs. The Indo/SE Asia route remained
the most active within the region, with ﬁxtures such as an SMX open KSC ﬁxing at mid USD 14k for Indo/Thai and another SMX open CTG ﬁxing around USD 12k dop
for Indo/Thai. Demand on the Indo/China route continued to be weak, particularly in North China, where limited cargo availability provided little support. Activity on
the Indo/India route also slowed, with reported ﬁxtures including an SMX open CTG ﬁxing around USD 16.5k for Indo/Bdesh and another SMX open Weda ﬁxing
around USD 21k for Indo/WCI, both reﬂecting a noticeable pullback from earlier peak levels.
Activity in the North Vietnam/South China region also declined, as most cargo laycans were scheduled for post-holiday periods, allowing charterers more ﬂexibility and
reducing urgency to ﬁx vessels. This led to a slight softening in freight levels. A visible bid/oﬀer gap persisted, with charterers bidding around USD 23k+ for UMX open
South China for clinker to ECI/Bdesh, while owners continued to hold ﬁrm at USD 27–28k levels, indicating intensiﬁed short-term negotiations. Meanwhile, nickel ore
shipments remained relatively stable, providing some underlying support, with SMX open South China ﬁxing around USD 17–18k for nickel ore to China.
The NOPAC market remained stable overall. Although activity was relatively limited, freight levels held ﬁrm, with UMX open Far East ﬁxtures still achieving USD 19k+ for
NOPAC round voyages, oﬀering a solid ﬂoor to the market.
North China steel and general cargo exports continued to command relatively high freight levels, particularly for vessels capable of transiting the Red Sea, which
attracted a premium. Reported ﬁxtures included a UMX open Tianjin on subs ﬁxing in the low USD 23k range to the Mediterranean via Goa. Regional trades also
remained active, with an SMX open North China ﬁxing at USD 18k+ to Southeast Asia. Bulk cargoes continued to provide support, with a UMX open Lanshan ﬁxing
around USD 21k dop for slag to Bdesh and another UMX open CJK on subs around USD 23.5k for petcoke to ECI, indicating that the overall market remained ﬁrm.
The Australian market maintained a steady performance this week, with consistent cargo ﬂow from the supply side. Grain and salt from Western Australia, coal from
Eastern Australia, and minerals from Northern Australia continued at a regular pace, supporting the regional market. Fixtures included a UMX open Jakarta ﬁxing
around USD 24k for Aus/China and a coastal UMX ﬁxing around USD 17k + USD 500k gbb for East Australia/China coal, indicating that freight levels remained relatively
high.
In the period market, a slight cooling was also observed, with charterers adopting a more cautious stance. UMX short period ﬁxtures were generally concluded in the
USD 19–20k range, depending on vessel position and speciﬁcations. Reported deals included an SMX open North China ﬁxing around USD 18.5k for two laden legs and
a UMX delivery Singapore ﬁxing in the low USD 20k range for a minimum of four months, showing a modest retreat from earlier highs.
Overall, after the recent rapid rally, the Paciﬁc Supramax market has entered a phase of consolidation, with momentum slowing but rates remaining at elevated levels.
In the short term, the anticipated release of additional cargoes after the holiday is expected to provide underlying support to the market. Going forward, close
attention should be paid to the pace of demand recovery post-holiday and the potential return of tonnage, both of which will inﬂuence the market balance.

$13.50 for a wider 07/16 May laycan. In addition, two stems discharging in Taiwan were ﬁxed, one a Nuke reportedly from Port Walcott at mid/high
$12s for a 17/21 May. Additionally, an operator’s tender out of Newcastle to Taiwan ﬁxed for spilt May dates at $20.32, contributing to healthy
volumes to start the week. One end user’s stem discharging in Taiwan from Port Walcott was ﬁxed on a Nuke in mid-high $12s for 17/21 May and
lastly a Paciﬁc round ﬁxed at $34,000 with delivery to Lanshan. Into Tuesday, activity in the Paciﬁc seemed strong from the get-go as three majors
were seen in the market. Owners promptly oﬀered very high $13s to $14 range to the Stanley Point major, who ended up ﬁxing a few mid-May C5
stems, with one known to be at $13.50. A Hedland major ﬁxed soon after at $13.10 and $13.15 for their mid May stems and the Dampier major was
reluctant to ﬁx on the day. Additionally, a Newcastlemax as reportedly ﬁxed at $38,500 for a West Australia round voyage. Out of Samarinda – the
usual operator ﬁxed their 04/10 May repositioning stem to Mundra in the low $10s. Meanwhile, headed into the middle of the week the Paciﬁc
remained strong as four majors were seen in the market this morning, demand in the Paciﬁc was well supported. It wasn’t long before oﬀers in the
mid-high 13s were promptly shown by owners. One Hedland major was reported to ﬁx in the mid $13s for their 12 May onwards C5 stem, whilst the
Stanley Point major ﬁxed 15/17 May C5 stem in the low $13s. Operator activity was strong as a couple of C5 stems each ﬁxed for 16/18 May dates at
$13.15-25, respectively. A couple of tenders to Korea from East Australia were seen to ﬁx for split May dates ranging from $21.21-27. All in all, the
basin looked to soften as charterers sharpened bids. Into the latter half of the week – the demand picture continued to show strength as four
majors were present. Oﬀers were quickly seen in the mid-high $13s from owners. However, majors seemed reluctant to engage at these levels early
on. Eventually, a Hedland major ﬁxed their 18/20 May C5 stem in the $13.40-45 region, whilst a second major ﬁxed at $13.99 for their stem from 14
May. Additionally One operator promptly bid $13 for a Newcastlemax for their 20/21 May C5 stem. Whilst another operator secured their 14/23 May
stem out of Newcastle on a TCT for redelivery to Dangjin, however rates remain unclear at this time. Into Friday, volumes were limited with several
countries on holiday. One major was in the market and ﬁxed directly at $13.65 for 18 May slot while an operator was seeking a Nuke for their 20-21
May slot - however, little engagement was reported.
The South Atlantic started the week with a healthy cargo list refreshed early on yet both sides were reluctant to engage. Stems ex South Africa saw
high $24s oﬀers for their mid-May laycans, however bids were less forthcoming. Early June vessels oﬀered $33 C3 on standards, whilst mid-June got
to low-mid $32’s on larger tonnage. Bids for the latter window sat closer to $31 – however, limited ﬁxing occurred. Into Tuesday, after a static start
to the week in the South Atlantic saw activity pick up as an operator’s South African stem from Richards Bay to India for 10/19 May was promptly
oﬀered high $16s before later ﬁxing, however rates remain elusive. Out of Brazil, charterers began amongst the $32.00-50 C3 range across later
May dates, whilst a German operator was seen bidding $31 C3 for their early June stem. However, owners remained resilient as oﬀers in the $33.00-
75 C3 range remained consistent, and soon Charterers began bidding high $32s to $33.Into the afternoon, a trader ﬁnally ﬁxed their slit dates stem
at $32.95 C3. Lastly, a Brazilian stem to Malaysia ﬁxed in the afternoon for split May/June dates at June C3 equivalent with a premium. Into the
middle of the week, bids were seen to improve throughout the day as charterers began pushing on price to encourage owners’ engagement. It
wasnt until the afternoon until a handful of ﬁxtures concluded with an owner securing two of their vessels from Brazil to China for end May dates at
$33.40-50 C3. Meanwhile, a Newcastlemax was suspected to have ﬁxed on an operator’s West African 20/25 May stem to China, rumoured to be in
excess of $34. Some excitement came after a miner’s 20/24 May tender from South Africa to Korea ﬁxed at $24.60. Into the latter half of the week -
positivity from last night trickled into this morning with several looking to move prior to the long weekend in several countries. The recently active
operator took a vessel ETA 31 May in Brazil at $34.75 C3 while the 01/10 June slot ﬁxed a couple of times around mid $34 C3. Additionally, the usual
trader out of Sudeste was rumored to have ﬁxed a Newcastlemax at low $35.00's C3. Meanwhile, out of South Africa the same miner out of
Saldanha Bay that ﬁxed on Wednesday came back to market and ﬁxed with the same Greek owners at $24.90. All in all, the South Atlantic saw
decent volumes as rates ﬁrmed. Into Friday, the basin ﬁrmed up as bid bids for early June were at mid $34.00's basis C3 while oﬀers were few. Into
next week, the basin remains seeing strong demand while ballaster supply remains moderate.
After a handful of stems were seen to ﬁx in the North on during the end of last week – thus, demand looked sparse heading into Monday. Two end
user’s fresh tenders were welcomed into the basin and oﬀered needed support heading further into the week. A fronthaul tender for split May &
June dates from Canada to Korea and a transatlantic tender from Brazil to Egypt for 16/30 May dates. West African stems to the Far East continued
to attract vessels stationed in the North as one vessel was ﬁxed from Nouadhibou to Qingdao for 15/24 May in the mid $33s on Tuesday which
when run back to C9 duration was at mid/high $60k. The middle the week welcomed some colour as a German owner’s Newcastlemax ﬁxed on a
16/30 May transatlantic tender from Brazil to Egypt – however, rates remained unclear. As the week came to a close, tonnage remained relatively
unchanged as few fresh stems oﬀered little support as a traders fronthaul remains for 24/30 May dates from Sept-Isles to China while an end user
returned to market with a 20/30 May transatlantic tender from Brazil to Egypt.

The ongoing tensions in the Middle East, particularly concerning the Strait of Hormuz,
have resulted in increased restrictions on the movement of tonnage, creating further un-
certainty across the commodity markets. Shortages within both the oil and gas sectors are
continuing to have a knock -on effect across the shipping industry, including the ship recy-
cling sector.

Despite these challenges, sentiment remains broadly positive, with enquiry continuing to
be seen across all of the Indian Sub Continent markets. Price levels do vary, with Bangla-
desh continuing to lead, followed by Pakistan, with India trailing, although the differential
is not particularly significant. India does, however, retain a clear advantage when it comes
to specialised and HKC -compliant tonnage, with virtually all recycling yards now fully com-
pliant.

The persistent issue remains the ongoing shortage of available tonnage, which has result-
ed in a slowdown in fresh sales, with previously concluded transactions once again coming
to the forefront of market reporting.

The sanctioned VLCC “Mali” (39,388 lwt), which had earlier been refused entry into Paki-
stan and was subsequently reported as heading towards Sharjah, has now arrived in
Alang, India. It is assumed that the vessel has now satisfied the enhanced documentary
requirements imposed by the local authorities and has been granted clearance in prepara-
tion for delivery.
Meanwhile, uncertainty continues to surround the two OFAC sanctioned VLCCs “Itaugua”
and “Shelif”, both of which were previously refused entry into Bangladesh. No confirmed
sales have yet been reported for either vessel, although market speculation has suggested
their presence offshore Chattogram. However, latest position data appears to contradict
this, with the “Shelif” currently reported at anchor in the Persian Gulf, while the “Itaugua”
is indicated to be in the South China Sea.

The Capesize “Jin Jiang” was originally reported sold for recycling in March, with the Own-
ers having secured the option to trade the vessel further prior to resale. Now renamed
“Jiang”, the vessel has surprisingly arrived in Bangladesh following a subsequent resale on
private terms. This change in direction is likely reflective of the significant improvement in
pricing seen in Bangladesh over the past month. No resale price has yet been disclosed.

Looking ahead, the market appears to be delicately balanced. While underlying demand
from recyclers remains firm and pricing has shown resilience, the lack of available ton-
nage continues to limit overall activity. Should supply begin to return, particularly in the
form of larger units, competition between yards could quickly intensify, supporting further
firming of price levels. Much will depend on the broader geopolitical backdrop; however, if
stability improves and owners regain confidence to release vessels, there remains poten-
tial for a more active and competitive market in the weeks ahead.

India’s Crude Oil Imports Fall To All -Time Low
India’s crude oil imports from the Middle East Gulf dropped by 1.95M b/d m -o-m and by 1.28M b/d y -o-y to 1.18M b/d in March, the
lowest on records dating back to 2012, according to Reuters tanker arrivals data. Shipments from North America and Latin Amer ica
also declined by 60K b/d m -o-m to 160K b/d and by 180K b/d m -o-m to 130K b/d respectively. Meanwhile, arrivals from the FSU
rose by 1.27M b/d m -o-m to 2.36M b/d, while volumes from West Africa grew by 130K b/d m -o-m to 500K b/d. Overall crude oil im-
ports fell by 800K b/d m -o-m to 4.49M b/d, an eight -month low.

ARA Gasoil Stocks Drop To Lowest Level Since August 2025
At the Amsterdam -Rotterdam -Antwerp (ARA) storage hub, gasoil stocks declined by 20KT w -o-w to 1.84MT during the week ending
30 April, the lowest since August 2025, according to data from Refinitiv. Meanwhile, jet fuel inventories also dropped by 30K T w-o-w
to 550KT, the lowest since March 2020, whereas gasoline stocks were up by 40KT w -o-w to 1.15MT. Total clean product stocks re-
mained relatively stable w -o-w at 3.93MT.

Fertilizer Markets Under Strain as Supply Disruptions Drive Volatility
Fertilizer markets remain under severe pressure as unresolved Middle East tensions and the Strait of Hormuz blockade reduce e ffec-
tive shipping volumes by an estimated 80 -90%, according to CRU. Bulk Ammonia prices continue to climb amid tight global supply,
up $13/t on the week to ~$890/t CFR NW Europe as of 30 April, according to CRU. Sulphur has recorded further triple -digit weekly
increases, up $105/t to ~$830/t CFR China. Urea prices have eased after India purchased 2.5 Mt for delivery through mid -June,
with bulk Urea FOB New Orleans price down $19/t to ~640/t in the week ending 30 April.

US Weekly Grain Exports
In the week to 23 April, US combined exports of corn, wheat, soy (beans and meal) and sorghum dipped 0.5 Mt from the prior we ek
to 3.2 Mt, USDA data show. This came as exports declined of corn ( -0.3 Mt to 1.6 Mt), wheat ( -0.1 Mt to 0.3 Mt) and soy
(beans+meal) ( -0.1 Mt to 1.0 Mt). Conversely, sorghum shipments remained near steady on the week at 0.2 Mt.

items.parsed_text: Panam ax/Kamsarmax Report1st May 2026 ATL: FLAT PAC: FIRM MID EAST: FLAT Market Comments ATL SHORT IN A WEEK CHARACTERIZED BY WIDE-SPREAD HOLIDAYS AND DRYBULK CONVENTIONS IN GENEVA WE RECORDED MARGINAL GAINS ON THE INDEX WITH AVERAGE EARNINGS CLOSING US$401 UP FROM THE START OF THE WEEK. FRONTHAUL ACTIVITY CONTINUES TO PROVIDE THE UNERLYING STRENGTH IN THE BASIN WITH GRAINS EX NCSA AND US COAL EXPORTS. P6 ACTIVITY LEVELS ARE DOWN BUT SUPPLY SIDE REMAINS TIGHT AND PACIFIC MARKET IS BOUYANT. PAC SHORT THE PACIFIC PANAMAX MARKET STRENGTHENED THIS WEEK DESPITE WIDESPREAD HOLIDAYS ACROSS THE REGION. DEMAND REMAINED FIRM—PARTICULARLY FOR MINERALS FROM EAST AUSTRALIA AND INDONESIA—DRIVING STEADY RATE INCREASES THROUGH THE WEEK. FFAS EDGED HIGHER, WHILE THE INDICES POSTED GAINS, WITH P3 RISING TO $19,667 AND P5 REACHING $20,467, ITS HIGHEST LEVEL SINCE JULY 2022. INDONESIA CONTINUED TO LEAD MARKET MOMENTUM, SUPPORTED BY STRONG CARGO VOLUMES AND IMPROVING FIXING LEVELS. EARLY IN THE WEEK, OVERAGE LME’S WERE FIXING AROUND $19–20K FOR SOUTH CHINA ROUNDS, RISING TO ABOUT $21K BY WEEK’S END. AUSTRALIA FOLLOWED A SIMILAR UPWARD TREND, WITH A HEALTHY CARGO LIST ALLOWING OWNERS TO SECURE PROGRESSIVELY STRONGER RATES. INDIA WAS RELATIVELY QUIET, THOUGH SOME ACTIVITY WAS REPORTED WITH RATES IN THE MID $19’S BKI RANGE FOR AUSSIE/INDIA RUNS. THE NOPAC MARKET SAW LIMITED ACTIVITY BUT STILL RECORDED MODEST IMPROVEMENTS, WITH RATES MOVING FROM THE MID-$17K RANGE TO LOW/MID-$18K LEVELS. MARKET ACTIVITY SLOWED FROM THURSDAY DUE TO HOLIDAYS ACROSS KEY REGIONS, BUT SENTIMENT REMAINS FIRM. LOOKING AHEAD, ALTHOUGH FURTHER HOLIDAYS MAY DAMPEN EARLY-WEEK ACTIVITY, SUSTAINED CARGO DEMAND AND HIGH OIL PRICES ARE EXPECTED TO SUPPORT RATES IN THE NEAR TERM Recent Fixtures ATLANTIC MV STAR TRADER (82/10) FIXED APS ECSA/SKAW-GIB $29,250 MV GUO YUAN 20 (75/12) KRISHNAPATNAM 30 APR FIXED ECSA/SGP-JPN GRAINS $19,250 PACIFIC MV CANON TRADER (82/24) RIZHAO SPOT FIXED NOPAC/SGP-JPN GRAINS $20,250 MV NICOLAUS SCHULTE (82/23) DALIAN 29 APRIL FXD EAUS/SGP-JPN COAL $21,000Baltic Routes Routes 24/04/26 01/05/26 P1A_82 Transatlantic RV 14,123 13,733 P2A_82 Cont-Far East 25,223 24,794 P3A_82 Transpacific RV 18,828 19,706 P4_82 Backhaul 13,363 13,890 P6_82 18,473 19,300 5TC Average 17,638 18,018 Physical Markets (All rates basis index type) Charterers Owners Transatlantic RV 13,000 15,000 NC Cont-Far East 24,000 27,000 - Transpacific RV 18,500 20,500 + Backhaul 13,000 15,000 NC Short period Atlantic* 21,000 23,000 + Short period Pacific 18,500 20,500 + 1 year Atlantic* 18,000 20,000 NC 1 year Pacific 17,000 18,000 - 2 years 15,500 16,500 - 3 years 15,000 16,000 - 5 years 14,250 16,250 NC *Redelivery worldwide Panamax 5 TC Average $/day Approximate Tonnage Supply/Demand (<20 years, for guidance only) Atlantic Pacific UKC MED StLaw USEC USG ECSA SAFR ME FE SEASIAUSNP/BC SupplySpot/10 days 15 22 1 1 1 18 11 72 62 111 28 10/30 days 9 14 1 1 2 6 2 35 28 35 28 DemandSpot/10 days 1 2 0 0 0 0 0 1 5 15 0 10/30 days 3 4 2 4 5 8 0 1 5 11 6 Simpson Spence Young Ltd T: +44 (0)20 7977 7400 E: panamax@ssyglobal.comWhile reasonable care has been taken to ensure that the information in this publication is accurate, SSY can accept no responsibility for any errors or omissions or any consequences arising therefrom. WHEREAS DEMAND AND SUPPLY APPEARED SOMEWHAT BALANCED AT THE START OF THE WEEK, AS WE PROGRESSED FRESH CARGO DEMAND BECAME LIMITED WITH LITTLE ENQUIRY FOR BOTH GRAINS AND MINERALS. CONSEQUENTLY WE SAW COSMETIC CORRECTION ON THIS ROUTE WEEK ON WEEK. MUCH OF THE ATTENTION WAS FOCUSED ON 2A EARNINGS. 2A MUCH OF THE ATLANTIC ACTIVITY WAS FOCUSED ON THE FRONTHUALS THIS WEEK DUE TO THE ELEVATED EARNINGS AND STABLE INFLUX OF CARGO DEMAND. NCSA GRAINS AND ALSO US COAL EXPORTS TO INDIA AND SOUTH EAST ASIA PROVIDDED MUCH OF THE SOURCE FOR THE SUPPORT ON THE FRONTHUALS. ALTHOUGH THE INDEX LEVELS HAVE TICKED UP AT THE END OF THE WEEK, EARNINGS ARE ACTUALLY MARGINALLY DOWN FROM THE START OF THE WEEK. CHARTERERS HAVE BEEN VERY DISCIPLINED AND SUCCESSFULLY BIDD SELECTIVELY AT WELL POSITIONED ECO KAMSARMAXES AT LEVELS IN THE LOW US$24'S EX GIBRALTAR. THE TONNAGE LIST IS WELL MANAGED FOR THE TIMEBEING WE EXPECT EARNINGS TO BE SUSTAINED IN THE NEARBY AT AROUND THE CURRENT LEVELS. P6 EARNINGS FOR EAST COAST SOUTH AMERICAN GRAINS HAVE TICKED UP MARGINALLY, PARTICULARLY IN THE SECOND HALF OF THE WEEK, HOWEVER ACTIVITY LEVELS ARE SUBDUED FOR THIS TIME OF THE YEAR. FFA'S HAVE NUDGED UP WITH MAY BID IMPROVING FROM $18,650 LAST FRIDAY TO $19,450 AT THE TIME OF WRITING. THE INDICES HAVE ALSO RISEN WITH P3 UP $839 FROM $18,828 LAST FRIDAY TO $19,667 LAST NIGHT. P5 MEANWHILE IS THE HIGHEST IT'S BEEN SINCE JULY 2022 HAVE IMPROVED $1,386 FROM $19,081 LAST FRIDAY TO $20,467. THE STRONG INDONESIA MARKET HAS CONTINUED THIS WEEK WITH ROBUST VOLUMES AND SUSTAINED IMPROVEMENTS IN FIXING LEVELS. OVERAGE LME'S OPEN SOUTH CHINA WERE FIXING AROUND $19-20K FOR ROUNDS BACK TO SOUTH CHINA ON MONDAY WITH A 74/01 OPEN SOUTH CHINA FIXED AT $20K, WHILE BY THE END OF THE WEEK WE SAW A 76/01 OPEN HK FIXED AT $21K. AUSTRALIA HAS FOLLOWED A SIMILAR PATH WITH A HEALTHY CARGO LIST AND OWNERS ABLE TO SECURE STRONGER RATES AS THE WEEK PROGRESSED. ON MONDAY AN 82/21 OPEN KOREA FIXED $21,500 ($19,800 BKI CJK) FOR AUSSIE/SCHINA AND AN 82/18 OPEN NORTH CHINA FIXED FOR THE SAME TRIP AT $20K ($19,750 BKI CJK). ON WEDNESDAY WE SAW AN 82/24 OPEN KOREAN FIXED AT $23K ($20,700 BKI CJK) AND AN 82/24 OPEN NORTH CHINA FIXED AT $23,500 ($20,250 BKI CJK). INDIA WAS RELATIVELY QUIET THIS WEEK, BUT WE DID HEAR OF A SCRUBBER KAMSARMAX OPEN NORTH CHINA FIXED AT $22K ($19,500 BKI CJK) FOR AUSSIE/INDIA BHP CARGO AND AN AN 82K VESSEL OPEN MID CHINA FIXED AT LOW $21'S (MID $19'S BKI) FOR THE SAME. NOPAC WAS PRETTY QUIET IN COMPARISON, BUT RATES ALSO IMPROVED ON THE FEW CARGOES WE HEARD COVERED. ON MONDAY WE HEARD RUMOURS OF A CHARTERER COVERING A NOPAC GRAINS AT MID $17'S BKI CJK ALTHOUGH FURTHER DETAILS WERE NOT AVAILABLE. WHILE ON WEDNESDAY WE HEARD OF A COUPLE OF KAMSARMAXES FIXED AT LOW/MID $18'S BKI CJK. WITH HOLIDAYS IN MANY OF THE USUAL SHIPPING HUBS (CHINA, SINGAPORE, HONG KONG, INDIA, INDONESIA, MALAYSIA, PHILIPPPINES, TAIWAN, GREECE ETC) TODAY THE MARKET QUIETENED OFF SIGNIFICANTLY FROM THURSDAY ONWARDS, BUT RATES REMAIN FIRM AS WE HEAD IN TO ANOTHER HOLIDAY DISRUPTED WEEK NEXT WEEK WITH JAPAN RETURNING TO THE OFFICE ON THURSDAY AND CHINA/KOREA ON WEDNESDAY. ALTHOUGH WE WILL LIKELY SEE A SLOW START DUE TO THE HOLIDAYS, WITH OIL PRICES REMAINING HIGH AND CARGO DEMAND CONSISTENT WE SEE NO REASON FOR RATES TO DROP IN THE SHORT TERM AT LEAST. INDIA WAS RELATIVELY QUIET THIS WEEK, BUT WE DID HEAR OF A SCRUBBER KAMSARMAX OPEN NORTH CHINA FIXED AT $22K ($19,500 BKI CJK) FOR AUSSIE/INDIA BHP CARGO AND AN AN 82K VESSEL OPEN MID CHINA FIXED AT LOW $21'S (MID $19'S BKI) FOR THE SAME. NOPAC WAS PRETTY QUIET IN COMPARISON, BUT RATES ALSO IMPROVED ON THE FEW CARGOES WE HEARD COVERED. ON MONDAY WE HEARD RUMOURS OF A CHARTERER COVERING A NOPAC GRAINS AT MID $17'S BKI CJK ALTHOUGH FURTHER DETAILS WERE NOT AVAILABLE. WHILE ON WEDNESDAY WE HEARD OF A COUPLE OF KAMSARMAXES FIXED AT LOW/MID $18'S BKI CJK. WITH HOLIDAYS IN MANY OF THE USUAL SHIPPING HUBS (CHINA, SINGAPORE, HONG KONG, INDIA, INDONESIA, MALAYSIA, PHILIPPPINES, TAIWAN, GREECE ETC) TODAY THE MARKET QUIETENED OFF SIGNIFICANTLY FROM THURSDAY ONWARDS, BUT RATES REMAIN FIRM AS WE HEAD IN TO ANOTHER HOLIDAY DISRUPTED WEEK NEXT WEEK WITH JAPAN RETURNING TO THE OFFICE ON THURSDAY AND CHINA/KOREA ON WEDNESDAY. ALTHOUGH WE WILL LIKELY SEE A SLOW START DUE TO THE HOLIDAYS, WITH OIL PRICES REMAINING HIGH AND CARGO DEMAND CONSISTENT WE SEE NO REASON FOR RATES TO DROP IN THE SHORT TERM AT LEAST. A steady start to the week in the Pacific, with two majors present and robust operator C5 and peripheral interest. Low $13 offers remained resilient, leading the Dampier major to take a few vessels for mid-May at $13 C5. Meanwhile, a Hedland majors concluded at $12.85 and an operator fixed the high of the day at $13.50 for a wider 07/16 May laycan. In addition, two stems discharging in Taiwan were fixed, one a Nuke reportedly from Port Walcott at mid/high $12s for a 17/21 May. Additionally, an operator’s tender out of Newcastle to Taiwan fixed for spilt May dates at $20.32, contributing to healthy volumes to start the week. One end user’s stem discharging in Taiwan from Port Walcott was fixed on a Nuke in mid-high $12s for 17/21 May and lastly a Pacific round fixed at $34,000 with delivery to Lanshan. Into Tuesday, activity in the Pacific seemed strong from the get-go as three majors were seen in the market. Owners promptly offered very high $13s to $14 range to the Stanley Point major, who ended up fixing a few mid-May C5 stems, with one known to be at $13.50. A Hedland major fixed soon after at $13.10 and $13.15 for their mid May stems and the Dampier major was reluctant to fix on the day. Additionally, a Newcastlemax as reportedly fixed at $38,500 for a West Australia round voyage. Out of Samarinda – the usual operator fixed their 04/10 May repositioning stem to Mundra in the low $10s. Meanwhile, headed into the middle of the week the Pacific remained strong as four majors were seen in the market this morning, demand in the Pacific was well supported. It wasn’t long before offers in the mid-high 13s were promptly shown by owners. One Hedland major was reported to fix in the mid $13s for their 12 May onwards C5 stem, whilst the Stanley Point major fixed 15/17 May C5 stem in the low $13s. Operator activity was strong as a couple of C5 stems each fixed for 16/18 May dates at $13.15-25, respectively. A couple of tenders to Korea from East Australia were seen to fix for split May dates ranging from $21.21-27. All in all, the basin looked to soften as charterers sharpened bids. Into the latter half of the week – the demand picture continued to show strength as four majors were present. Offers were quickly seen in the mid-high $13s from owners. However, majors seemed reluctant to engage at these levels early on. Eventually, a Hedland major fixed their 18/20 May C5 stem in the $13.40-45 region, whilst a second major fixed at $13.99 for their stem from 14 May. Additionally One operator promptly bid $13 for a Newcastlemax for their 20/21 May C5 stem. Whilst another operator secured their 14/23 May stem out of Newcastle on a TCT for redelivery to Dangjin, however rates remain unclear at this time. Into Friday, volumes were limited with several countries on holiday. One major was in the market and fixed directly at $13.65 for 18 May slot while an operator was seeking a Nuke for their 20-21 May slot - however, little engagement was reported. The South Atlantic started the week with a healthy cargo list refreshed early on yet both sides were reluctant to engage. Stems ex South Africa saw high $24s offers for their mid-May laycans, however bids were less forthcoming. Early June vessels offered $33 C3 on standards, whilst mid-June got to low-mid $32’s on larger tonnage. Bids for the latter window sat closer to $31 – however, limited fixing occurred. Into Tuesday, after a static start to the week in the South Atlantic saw activity pick up as an operator’s South African stem from Richards Bay to India for 10/19 May was promptly offered high $16s before later fixing, however rates remain elusive. Out of Brazil, charterers began amongst the $32.00-50 C3 range across later May dates, whilst a German operator was seen bidding $31 C3 for their early June stem. However, owners remained resilient as offers in the $33.00- 75 C3 range remained consistent, and soon Charterers began bidding high $32s to $33.Into the afternoon, a trader finally fixed their slit dates stem at $32.95 C3. Lastly, a Brazilian stem to Malaysia fixed in the afternoon for split May/June dates at June C3 equivalent with a premium. Into the middle of the week, bids were seen to improve throughout the day as charterers began pushing on price to encourage owners’ engagement. It wasnt until the afternoon until a handful of fixtures concluded with an owner securing two of their vessels from Brazil to China for end May dates at $33.40-50 C3. Meanwhile, a Newcastlemax was suspected to have fixed on an operator’s West African 20/25 May stem to China, rumoured to be in excess of $34. Some excitement came after a miner’s 20/24 May tender from South Africa to Korea fixed at $24.60. Into the latter half of the week - positivity from last night trickled into this morning with several looking to move prior to the long weekend in several countries. The recently active operator took a vessel ETA 31 May in Brazil at $34.75 C3 while the 01/10 June slot fixed a couple of times around mid $34 C3. Additionally, the usual trader out of Sudeste was rumored to have fixed a Newcastlemax at low $35.00's C3. Meanwhile, out of South Africa the same miner out of Saldanha Bay that fixed on Wednesday came back to market and fixed with the same Greek owners at $24.90. All in all, the South Atlantic saw decent volumes as rates firmed. Into Friday, the basin firmed up as bid bids for early June were at mid $34.00's basis C3 while offers were few. Into next week, the basin remains seeing strong demand while ballaster supply remains moderate. After a handful of stems were seen to fix in the North on during the end of last week – thus, demand looked sparse heading into Monday. Two end user’s fresh tenders were welcomed into the basin and offered needed support heading further into the week. A fronthaul tender for split May & June dates from Canada to Korea and a transatlantic tender from Brazil to Egypt for 16/30 May dates. West African stems to the Far East continued to attract vessels stationed in the North as one vessel was fixed from Nouadhibou to Qingdao for 15/24 May in the mid $33s on Tuesday which when run back to C9 duration was at mid/high $60k. The middle the week welcomed some colour as a German owner’s Newcastlemax fixed on a 16/30 May transatlantic tender from Brazil to Egypt – however, rates remained unclear. As the week came to a close, tonnage remained relatively unchanged as few fresh stems offered little support as a traders fronthaul remains for 24/30 May dates from Sept-Isles to China while an end user returned to market with a 20/30 May transatlantic tender from Brazil to Egypt. Bulk Ammonia prices continue to climb amid tight global supply, up $13/t on the week to ~$890/t CFR NW Europe as of 30 April, according to CRU. Sulphur has recorded further triple-digit weekly increases, up $105/t to ~$830/t CFR China. Urea prices have eased after India purchased 2.5 Mt for delivery through mid-June, with bulk Urea FOB New Orleans price down $19/t to ~640/t in the week ending 30 April. US Weekly Grain Exports In the week to 23 April, US combined exports of corn, wheat, soy (beans and meal) and sorghum dipped 0.5 Mt from the prior week to 3.2 Mt, USDA data show. This came as exports declined of corn (-0.3 Mt to 1.6 Mt), wheat (-0.1 Mt to 0.3 Mt) and soy (beans+meal) (-0.1 Mt to 1.0 Mt). items.parsed_text: Handysize/Supramax Report1st May 2026 63,500 Atlantic: SOFTER Pacific: FIRM 38,000 Atlantic: FLAT Pacific: FLAT Atlantic Comment The Baltic Dry Index (BDI) has extended its upward trajectory to close out April, hovering near 2,670 points and driven by a robust Capesize segment where daily earnings remain exceptionally high at over $35,000. The market's upward momentum is supported by strong iron ore and mineral flows from both the Atlantic and Pacific basins ahead of the May Day holidays. However, the operational reality for shipowners remains volatile as bunker fuel prices act like a rollercoaster, swinging wildly in response to fluctuating crude prices and ongoing Middle East tensions, meaning that these strong headline freight revenues are being continually squeezed by the unpredictable cost of refueling. In the Continent Handysize market, the week opened with a quiet start and activity has remained limited since. Fixing levels for a transatlantic voyage have stayed flat at $9,000, the same level as last week. For the Supramax and Ultramax sizes, rates have held firm, supported by a relatively tight tonnage list, with fixing levels for a transatlantic voyage up from last week at $10,500. The Mediterranean market has seen rates remain largely flat overall with little fresh enquiry failing to match a long tonnage list for both the smaller and larger sizes. While fixture volume has been thin, we heard that a 35k deadweight vessel fix basis Annaba for a trip to Malaysia for region $10,500 – 11,000. For the larger sizes, activity remained subdued, but despite this, fixing levels for a transatlantic voyage held firm at $10,500, up slightly from last week. The East Coast South America (ECSA) Handysize market firmed up noticeably again this week, though the recent momentum risks outpacing actual demand as owners push their rate expectations too far. While sentiment remains robust, a noticeable lack of fresh cargoes has created a disconnect, leaving charterers hesitant to meet the elevated levels being requested. Furthermore, a lingering supply of available vessels remains visible across the basin, meaning owners' attempts to push for higher rates may prove overextended. Unless fresh inquiries enter the market to absorb the remaining prompt tonnage, the recent firmness could stall, creating a more balanced or even softening environment as the week draws to a close. The ECSA and West Africa (WAFR) Supramax and Ultramax market is easing slightly moving into mid-May. While steady Brazilian grain and mineral flows provide some underlying support, charterers are successfully testing lower levels against the weight of the current tonnage overhang. In the West Africa region, the market remains somewhat positional. Ultramax units fixing from West Africa to the Continent are currently achieving between $17,000 and $17,500, while fronthaul routes are holding a relatively firmer tone, yielding between $21,000 and $22,000. Meanwhile, ECSA rates have softened. Fixtures to the Continent have slipped to around $24,500 though business directed toward the East Mediterranean is holding up slightly better, ranging closer to $27,000 to $27,500. Overall, the market remains on a mild downward trend, and its next direction will depend on fresh cargo volumes stepping in to absorb the available supply. It's been a fairly quiet week in the USG Handy Market. Rates have remained largely sideways, however there is underlying positive sentiment as we could potentially see an increase in tonnage/cargo next week as people return from holidays and the Geneva Dry Conference. The USG Smx market has lethargically drawn to a close after a flat week. Geneva Dry took a good chunk of players out the game and rates have been slowly tailing off after some strong transatlantic numbers reported on Monday. We saw a 64 deadweight vessel fix basis Mississippi River for a trip with grains to Spain at for $28,000. We have seen more fronthaul cargoes in the market this week, a mixture of grains and minerals. Nice Japanese Ultras have covered around the $24,000 level over the last few days whilst TA cargos have been less abundant than in previous weeks. A lot of operators are using own tonnage for their cargos and the tonnage counts indicate we will see excess tonnage supply for 1h May which will impact the rates negatively. The release of fresh cargoes was relatively limited, and with the approaching Labor Day holiday, charterers turned more cautious, leading to a noticeable cooling in the aggressive tonnage-fixing sentiment. While owners generally remained confident, some prompt vessels softened their offers slightly to secure employment. As a result, the market experienced a mild correction rather than any sharp downturn, and overall levels remained elevated. The Indonesian coal sector softened this week, with fewer fresh cargoes entering the market and rates easing from previous highs. The Indo/SE Asia route remained the most active within the region, with fixtures such as an SMX open KSC fixing at mid USD 14k for Indo/Thai and another SMX open CTG fixing around USD 12k dop for Indo/Thai. Demand on the Indo/China route continued to be weak, particularly in North China, where limited cargo availability provided little support. Activity on the Indo/India route also slowed, with reported fixtures including an SMX open CTG fixing around USD 16.5k for Indo/Bdesh and another SMX open Weda fixing around USD 21k for Indo/WCI, both reflecting a noticeable pullback from earlier peak levels. Activity in the North Vietnam/South China region also declined, as most cargo laycans were scheduled for post-holiday periods, allowing charterers more flexibility and reducing urgency to fix vessels. This led to a slight softening in freight levels. A visible bid/offer gap persisted, with charterers bidding around USD 23k+ for UMX open South China for clinker to ECI/Bdesh, while owners continued to hold firm at USD 27–28k levels, indicating intensified short-term negotiations. Meanwhile, nickel ore shipments remained relatively stable, providing some underlying support, with SMX open South China fixing around USD 17–18k for nickel ore to China. The NOPAC market remained stable overall. Although activity was relatively limited, freight levels held firm, with UMX open Far East fixtures still achieving USD 19k+ for NOPAC round voyages, offering a solid floor to the market. North China steel and general cargo exports continued to command relatively high freight levels, particularly for vessels capable of transiting the Red Sea, which attracted a premium. Reported fixtures included a UMX open Tianjin on subs fixing in the low USD 23k range to the Mediterranean via Goa. Regional trades also remained active, with an SMX open North China fixing at USD 18k+ to Southeast Asia. Bulk cargoes continued to provide support, with a UMX open Lanshan fixing around USD 21k dop for slag to Bdesh and another UMX open CJK on subs around USD 23.5k for petcoke to ECI, indicating that the overall market remained firm. The Australian market maintained a steady performance this week, with consistent cargo flow from the supply side. Grain and salt from Western Australia, coal from Eastern Australia, and minerals from Northern Australia continued at a regular pace, supporting the regional market. Fixtures included a UMX open Jakarta fixing around USD 24k for Aus/China and a coastal UMX fixing around USD 17k + USD 500k gbb for East Australia/China coal, indicating that freight levels remained relatively high. In the period market, a slight cooling was also observed, with charterers adopting a more cautious stance. UMX short period fixtures were generally concluded in the USD 19–20k range, depending on vessel position and specifications. Reported deals included an SMX open North China fixing around USD 18.5k for two laden legs and a UMX delivery Singapore fixing in the low USD 20k range for a minimum of four months, showing a modest retreat from earlier highs. Overall, after the recent rapid rally, the Pacific Supramax market has entered a phase of consolidation, with momentum slowing but rates remaining at elevated levels. In the short term, the anticipated release of additional cargoes after the holiday is expected to provide underlying support to the market. Going forward, close attention should be paid to the pace of demand recovery post-holiday and the potential return of tonnage, both of which will influence the market balance. Readers will note the same Owners recently acquired the Ex “THERESA HAINAN” (82k dwt 2013 Sainty Shipbuilding) at USD 16.8 mill. There have been two sales in the Supramax sector this week. Concluding this week's Dry Bulk news, the Handysize "BRAVE STAR" (38k dwt, 2019 Kanda - Log Fitted) has been sold at USD 28.5 mill basis a 3 - year BBHP structure. Readers will note that the same owners disposed of the Ex "DILONG SPIRIT" (159k dwt 2009 Bohai) in January at USD 42.5 mill to clients of IMS. Following last week’s sale of the "PUSAKA BORNEO" (108k dwt 2018 Tsu- neishi - Scrubber Fitted) at USD 76 mill to Greek interests, the sistership from separate Japanese Owners, namely the "SOUTHERN REVER- ENCE" (108k dwt 2018 Tsuneishi - Scrubber Fitted) invited offers on the 28th of April and is now rumoured sold at USD 75 mill. For reference, the year - older "STI BROOKLYN" & "STI BLACK HAWK" (50k dwt 2015 SPP/HMD, Epoxy - ME Engine / Scrubber Fitted) were sold end of March this year at USD 35 mill each. 0102030405060 Jan-22 Apr-22 Jul-22 Oct-22 Jan-23 Apr-23 Jul-23 Oct-23 Jan-24 Apr-24 Jul-24 Oct-24 Jan-25 Apr-25 Jul-25 Oct-25 Jan-26 Apr-26$k/day Cape 180kdwt Cape 182kdwt Panamax 82kdwt Supramax 63kdwt Handysize 38kdwt Source: Baltic Exchange Sale and Purchase Weekly Market Report BSRA Delivery Bangladesh (US$/LDT) Delivery India (US$/LDT) Tankers (LDT) 30001 & above 486.750 442.667 15001 - 30000 488.625 448.625 7000 - 15000 490.417 452.000 Bulkers (LDT) 20001 & above 473.167 429.250 9001 - 20000 477.000 437.667 5000 - 9000 476.083 439.000 Baltic Recycling Assessments Aframax earnings (non -eco, non -scrubber) Source: Baltic Exchange Source: SSY 1st May 2026 The ongoing tensions in the Middle East, particularly concerning the Strait of Hormuz, have resulted in increased restrictions on the movement of tonnage, creating further un- certainty across the commodity markets. Shortages within both the oil and gas sectors are continuing to have a knock -on effect across the shipping industry, including the ship recy- cling sector. Despite these challenges, sentiment remains broadly positive, with enquiry continuing to be seen across all of the Indian Sub Continent markets. Price levels do vary, with Bangla- desh continuing to lead, followed by Pakistan, with India trailing, although the differential is not particularly significant. India does, however, retain a clear advantage when it comes to specialised and HKC -compliant tonnage, with virtually all recycling yards now fully com- pliant. The persistent issue remains the ongoing shortage of available tonnage, which has result- ed in a slowdown in fresh sales, with previously concluded transactions once again coming to the forefront of market reporting. The sanctioned VLCC “Mali” (39,388 lwt), which had earlier been refused entry into Paki- stan and was subsequently reported as heading towards Sharjah, has now arrived in Alang, India. It is assumed that the vessel has now satisfied the enhanced documentary requirements imposed by the local authorities and has been granted clearance in prepara- tion for delivery. Meanwhile, uncertainty continues to surround the two OFAC sanctioned VLCCs “Itaugua” and “Shelif”, both of which were previously refused entry into Bangladesh. No confirmed sales have yet been reported for either vessel, although market speculation has suggested their presence offshore Chattogram. However, latest position data appears to contradict this, with the “Shelif” currently reported at anchor in the Persian Gulf, while the “Itaugua” is indicated to be in the South China Sea. The Capesize “Jin Jiang” was originally reported sold for recycling in March, with the Own- ers having secured the option to trade the vessel further prior to resale. Now renamed “Jiang”, the vessel has surprisingly arrived in Bangladesh following a subsequent resale on private terms. This change in direction is likely reflective of the significant improvement in pricing seen in Bangladesh over the past month. No resale price has yet been disclosed. Looking ahead, the market appears to be delicately balanced. While underlying demand from recyclers remains firm and pricing has shown resilience, the lack of available ton- nage continues to limit overall activity. Should supply begin to return, particularly in the form of larger units, competition between yards could quickly intensify, supporting further firming of price levels. Much will depend on the broader geopolitical backdrop; however, if stability improves and owners regain confidence to release vessels, there remains poten- tial for a more active and competitive market in the weeks ahead. Shortages within both the oil and gas sectors are continuing to have a knock -on effect across the shipping industry, including the ship recy- cling sector. Despite these challenges, sentiment remains broadly positive, with enquiry continuing to be seen across all of the Indian Sub Continent markets. Price levels do vary, with Bangla- desh continuing to lead, followed by Pakistan, with India trailing, although the differential is not particularly significant. India does, however, retain a clear advantage when it comes to specialised and HKC -compliant tonnage, with virtually all recycling yards now fully com- pliant. The persistent issue remains the ongoing shortage of available tonnage, which has result- ed in a slowdown in fresh sales, with previously concluded transactions once again coming to the forefront of market reporting. The sanctioned VLCC “Mali” (39,388 lwt), which had earlier been refused entry into Paki- stan and was subsequently reported as heading towards Sharjah, has now arrived in Alang, India. It is assumed that the vessel has now satisfied the enhanced documentary requirements imposed by the local authorities and has been granted clearance in prepara- tion for delivery. Meanwhile, uncertainty continues to surround the two OFAC sanctioned VLCCs “Itaugua” and “Shelif”, both of which were previously refused entry into Bangladesh. No confirmed sales have yet been reported for either vessel, although market speculation has suggested their presence offshore Chattogram. However, latest position data appears to contradict this, with the “Shelif” currently reported at anchor in the Persian Gulf, while the “Itaugua” is indicated to be in the South China Sea. The Capesize “Jin Jiang” was originally reported sold for recycling in March, with the Own- ers having secured the option to trade the vessel further prior to resale. Now renamed “Jiang”, the vessel has surprisingly arrived in Bangladesh following a subsequent resale on private terms. This change in direction is likely reflective of the significant improvement in pricing seen in Bangladesh over the past month. No resale price has yet been disclosed. Looking ahead, the market appears to be delicately balanced. While underlying demand from recyclers remains firm and pricing has shown resilience, the lack of available ton- nage continues to limit overall activity. Should supply begin to return, particularly in the form of larger units, competition between yards could quickly intensify, supporting further firming of price levels. Much will depend on the broader geopolitical backdrop; however, if stability improves and owners regain confidence to release vessels, there remains poten- tial for a more active and competitive market in the weeks ahead. ai_analysis.summary: 2026年5月1日波罗的海干散货指数收于2730点（+44），好望角型船领涨市场（BCI+120至4447），大西洋及太平洋航线需求稳健，尤其是C3及C5航线受南大西洋及澳大利亚煤炭出口支撑；巴拿马型船稳中有升（P2A+319），灵便型基本持平。FFA曲线近月合约升水明显，市场情绪偏多但受假期因素抑制活动。

sections.title: Market Structure
sections.content: 好望角型船延续强势，BCI 5TC达40331美元，太平洋市场情绪积极，C3航线受南大西洋货源支撑；巴拿马型船情绪转正，澳大利亚煤炭出口保持强劲；灵便型船活动平淡，吨位供应充足压制涨幅。FFA曲线呈近月升水结构，5月合约较即期溢价显著。

sections.title: Dry Bulk Signals
sections.content: 好望角型船：C5航线升至13.667，C3航线35.050，西澳至青岛航线供应趋紧；巴拿马型船：P2A涨至24794美元，北大陆和西地中海可用运力收紧；灵便型船：基本持平，美湾吨位充足抑制上涨。FFA市场做多情绪支撑近月合约。

sections.title: Trading Focus
sections.content: 关注C3航线南大西洋货源持续性及太平洋C5航线-ballaster供应；P2A关注北大陆吨位收紧能否传导至跨大西洋运价；FFA 5月好望角型合约在36350-36500区间可逢低布局；Cape/Jun差价扩大至2250美元关注套利机会。

market_watch: 好望角型船远期曲线近月溢价扩大，5月合约领涨，6月合约同步跟涨
巴拿马型船P5TC升至18018美元，澳大利亚煤炭出口强劲支撑太平洋市场
C3航线大西洋端报价坚挺，mid-$34至$35区间成交活跃
FFA市场做多情绪浓厚，Cape 5月合约突破36300阻力位
假期因素导致短期活动放缓，但基本面支撑运价上行
